fletcher-henderson__jazz-age: Before anyone said 'swing', Fletcher Henderson's Roseland Ballroom orchestra was inventing it — call-and-response brass, written arrangements with room to blow. A young Louis Armstrong passed through this band in 1924 and changed how everyone in it thought about time.
benny-goodman__bluebird-s-best-the-king-: When Goodman's band hit the Palomar Ballroom in August 1935, the kids at the front asked for the hot Fletcher Henderson arrangements — and the Swing Era officially began. Goodman also broke the colour bar, hiring Teddy Wilson and Lionel Hampton for his small groups.
benny-goodman__best-of-the-big-bands-vol: Columbia-era Goodman: the disciplined, driving big band at the height of its fame, a few years after the 1938 Carnegie Hall concert made jazz respectable to people who owned opera glasses.
billie-holiday__legends: Holiday recorded with Teddy Wilson's pick-up groups for the jukebox trade — cheap sessions, first takes, no rehearsal — and turned them into some of the most emotionally precise singing ever put on shellac. She stands a beat behind the band and makes you lean in.
coleman-hawkins__ultimate-coleman-hawkin: Hawkins effectively invented the tenor saxophone as a jazz voice, and his 1939 'Body and Soul' — two choruses that barely state the melody — is the record every saxophonist since has had to answer. Sonny Rollins picked the tracks on this set; that's a disciple choosing scripture.
eric-dolphy__the-essential-eric-dolphy: Dolphy took the alto, flute and bass clarinet somewhere nobody had mapped — intervals so wide they sound like questions. He died in Berlin in 1964 at 36; Coltrane kept his photograph on the wall.
elvis-presley__elvis-30-1-hits: The catalogue argument in one sitting: from 'Heartbreak Hotel' (1956) to 'Burning Love' (1972), thirty singles that each went to number one somewhere. The 2002 JXL remix of 'A Little Less Conversation' put him back at No.1 in the UK 25 years after his death.
diana-ross-the-supremes__40-golden-motow: Hitsville U.S.A. was a house on West Grand Boulevard, Detroit, with a studio in the garage and a sign that said what it meant. The Supremes were its flagship: twelve US number ones, the Funk Brothers playing on everything, quality control run like the car plants half the staff had left.
aretha-franklin__aretha-s-gold: Columbia spent six years not knowing what to do with Aretha Franklin. Atlantic flew her to Muscle Shoals in 1967, sat her at the piano, and got 'I Never Loved a Man' in an afternoon. This set collects the two-year eruption that followed — 'Respect', 'Chain of Fools', 'Think'.
al-green__love-happiness-the-very-best-o: Willie Mitchell built the Hi Records sound at Royal Studios, Memphis — drums soft as breath, strings, and Green floating over the top of it. Arguably the last great refinement of Southern soul before disco changed the rules.
curtis-mayfield__the-very-best-of-curtis: Mayfield left The Impressions, founded his own label, and made street-level social realism you could dance to. 'Move On Up' and the Super Fly soundtrack showed that message music and hit music didn't have to be different records.
black-sabbath__paranoid: Recorded in about six days in 1970. The title track was knocked out in half an hour as filler; 'War Pigs' and 'Iron Man' invented the vocabulary an entire genre still speaks. Four factory-town kids from Aston, Birmingham — heavy metal's birth certificate.
faces__first-step: The Small Faces minus Steve Marriott, plus Rod Stewart and Ronnie Wood — loose, boozy, and warmer than almost any band of their era. The Faces never quite made the perfect album; they made the perfect band instead.
ac-dc__high-voltage: Recorded at Albert Studios, Sydney, produced by Harry Vanda and George Young — older brother of Angus and Malcolm. No frills, no keyboards, no ballads: the template AC/DC would then refuse to change for fifty years, correctly.
ac-dc__dirty-deeds-done-dirt-cheap: The title came from a cartoon character's business card. Bon Scott's leering wit at full strength — Atlantic Records in America initially rejected the album, which tells you everything about how far ahead of the market they were.
ac-dc__let-there-be-rock: Reportedly the amps were smoking during the title track's final take and George Young waved the band on rather than stop it. The most live-sounding studio record of the '70s hard rock boom.
buzzcocks__love-bites: Punk's great romantics: Pete Shelley wrote about longing and embarrassment while everyone else wrote about the Queen. Contains 'Ever Fallen in Love...', the best pop single the punk movement produced.
buzzcocks__singles-going-steady: Originally a US-only compilation, now routinely cited among the greatest singles collections ever assembled. Buzzcocks also matter for how they started: they put on the Sex Pistols' Manchester gig and self-released their debut EP — the 'do it yourself' in DIY.
the-specials__the-singles-collection: 2 Tone Records, Coventry: ska revival as multi-racial protest pop. 'Ghost Town' went to No.1 in July 1981 while British cities were literally burning — the rare record that is also a news report.
bob-marley__legend: The best-selling reggae album ever made, assembled by Island in 1984 three years after Marley's death. The songs came out of Kingston yards and Island's London studios — 'No Woman, No Cry' credits a friend's soup kitchen so the royalties would keep it open.
david-bowie__space-oddity: Released nine days before Apollo 11 launched; the BBC used it in moon-landing coverage before anyone checked what happens to Major Tom. Bowie's first hit and first reinvention — there would be roughly one per album from here on.
david-bowie__hunky-dory: Written at the piano rather than the guitar — 'Changes', 'Life on Mars?', 'Queen Bitch' — with Rick Wakeman playing for session rates. Bowie called it the album that gave him the confidence to invent Ziggy six months later.
david-bowie__diamond-dogs: Bowie's Orwell musical after the Orwell estate said no: '1984', 'Big Brother', and a glam apocalypse he played guitar on himself, having just dissolved the Spiders from Mars. The bridge between glitter and the soul records that followed.
david-bowie__young-americans: 'Plastic soul', by his own description — cut at Sigma Sound in Philadelphia with a young Luther Vandross singing backup, and 'Fame' co-written with John Lennon during a night in New York. It gave Bowie his first American No.1.
david-bowie__let-s-dance: Nile Rodgers produced, Stevie Ray Vaughan played lead, and Bowie became a stadium act. He later had complicated feelings about the compromise; the grooves have no such doubts.
duran-duran__decade: Birmingham's Rum Runner club to yachts in Antigua in about three years — the New Romantic promise fulfilled. Duran Duran understood before almost anyone that in the MTV age the video was not an advert for the song; it was half the song.
beastie-boys__licensed-to-ill: The first rap album to top the Billboard chart, produced by Rick Rubin in Def Jam's NYU-dorm era, built on Zeppelin drums and brattiness the band spent the rest of their career apologising for — and outgrowing in public, which was the more interesting show.
beastie-boys__paul-s-boutique: Rejected on release, now a monument: the Dust Brothers layered hundreds of samples into something no clearance department would ever permit again. The 'Sgt. Pepper of hip-hop' claim gets made about once a week, and it holds.
beastie-boys__check-your-head: They picked their instruments back up — Money Mark on keys, hardcore roots showing — and stitched punk, funk and hip-hop into one room sound at their own G-Son studio in LA. The reinvention that made them permanent.
beastie-boys__hello-nasty: Made after Adam Yauch's Buddhist turn and the band's move back to New York; Grand Royal at its peak, 'Intergalactic' robot-dancing through Tokyo. Won the 1999 Grammy for Best Alternative Album — a category that tells you how uncategorisable they'd become.
depeche-mode__violator: Basildon synth-pop grown into black-leather stadium blues: 'Personal Jesus' and 'Enjoy the Silence', Flood co-producing. The album launch at a Los Angeles record store drew a crowd so large it became a police incident — for a synthesizer band from Essex.
blur__parklife: Recorded at Maison Rouge in Fulham while Britpop assembled itself around them. A concept album about English ordinariness — dog tracks, bank holidays, Phil Daniels narrating — that went four-times platinum and set up the Blur/Oasis front-page war of 1995.
daft-punk__homework: Two Parisians who'd been slated in Melody Maker as 'daft punk' took the insult as a name and made French house's founding document, largely in a bedroom on home equipment — hence the title. 'Da Funk' and 'Around the World' still sound like the future they predicted.
fatboy-slim__better-living-through-chemi: Norman Cook's fourth or fifth musical identity — ex-Housemartins bassist reborn as Brighton's big beat ringleader on Skint Records, gluing breakbeats to anything with a hook. The blueprint for the block-party sound that ate the late '90s.
amy-winehouse__frank: Nineteen years old, signed to Island, jazz chops from the National Youth Jazz Orchestra and a lyric sheet that took prisoners. Named for Sinatra; the talent is already fully formed, three years before Back to Black made her the biggest voice of her decade.
billie-holiday__me-myself-and-i: Mid-'30s Holiday with the Teddy Wilson units — Lester Young drifting in and out behind her, the two of them inventing a way of phrasing together that jazz singers and horn players have been borrowing from ever since.
beastie-boys__some-old-bullshit: The receipts: the Beasties' early-'80s hardcore EPs, when they were a teenage punk band playing New York matinees. Issued by the band themselves in 1994 with a title that reviews the contents honestly.
